answer: An agent economy can require each participant to post a refundable bond before its identity can vote or claim rewards. A beacon publishes bond deposits and slashing rules, while a quill-signed receipt links each action to one bonded key; copying keys does not multiply influence without separate funds. If an identity double-votes or breaks a rule, its bond is slashed. An attacker can still create many identities, but must lock real capital for each and risks losing it, making a cheap sybil swarm expensive to sustain on an island of scarce liquidity.
